text: Mary Renetta Hawton (née Bevis; 4 September 1924 – 18 January 1981) was an Australian tennis player whose career spanned the 1940s and 1950s. She won the women's doubles title at the Australian Championships five times and, in 1958, also secured the mixed doubles title with her compatriot Robert Howe. In 1948, she married Keith Ernest Hawton. Hawton served as captain of the Australian Fed Cup team in 1979 and 1980 and held the position of director at the NSW Tennis Association. In 1979, she published a book titled How to Play Winning Tennis. She passed away on 18 January 1981 in Sydney, Australia. The Mary Hawton Trophy, awarded to the winner of the Australian girls' team championships, and Hawton Place in the Canberra suburb of Chisholm, are both named in her honor. Hawton achieved significant success in Australia at the Australian Championships, reaching the semifinals in singles six times in 1948, 1952, 1953, 1954, 1956, and 1959, and reaching 12 finals, eight of which were consecutive. She also reached the doubles finals at Wimbledon and the French Championships in 1957 and 1958, partnering with Australian player Thelma Coyne Long. Hawton concluded her career with six Grand Slam titles: five in women's doubles and one in mixed doubles.
